posts.headline: Four ways DPDP quietly breaks your cloud architecture.
posts.lede: And what it costs to fix each one after the fact.

slides.title: Cross-border backups
slides.body: Your DR region is in Singapore. Under DPDP that is a transfer, not a backup. Re-siting DR mid-contract is the single most expensive fix we see.

slides.title: The offshore control plane
slides.body: Data at rest in Mumbai, orchestration in Virginia. Auditors read the control plane as processing. Most teams find this in month nine.

slides.title: Third-party SaaS in the path
slides.body: Every observability, logging and support tool touching personal data inherits your obligations. Average enterprise stack: 14 such tools.

slides.title: Consent as an afterthought
slides.body: Retrofitting consent state into a data model designed without it is a schema migration, not a feature. Budget quarters, not sprints.

slides.title: Design stage
slides.body: Residency built into the target architecture before a single workload moves. Incremental cost is design time only.

slides.title: Build stage
slides.body: Caught during migration. Re-siting DR and relocating the control plane while workloads are in flight.

slides.title: Post go-live
slides.body: Found by an internal review. Re-architecture plus full data revalidation, with production running.

slides.title: Post-audit finding
slides.body: Remediation under a clock, with regulatory exposure priced in. This is where the budget conversation stops being technical.
